title: DC-area forecast: Gradual clearing as temperatures climb this week
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Increased breaks in the clouds through evening as temperatures fall through the 60s.

What’s next? Generally pleasant weather Tuesday through Thursday as highs warm from the 70s into the 80s. Turning cooler into the weekend.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Turning partly cloudy and pleasant, with lows slipping to around 55 to 60 most spots, right near 60 in downtown DC. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Tuesday): Overall, it’s a good-looking day with partial sun, but a weak front passing through could bring a period of mostly cloudy skies and even a shower. It’s warmer, with highs in the mid-70s for most. Winds are light from the northwest. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Skies become mostly clear, and it’s a nice night. Lows range from the upper 50s to low 60s. Confidence: Medium-High

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

The warming trend continues Wednesday and Thursday, with both days featuring a good deal of sun. Highs are near 80 Wednesday and in the mid- to upper 80s Thursday. You’ll also notice a touch of humidity, with dew points rising into the 60s. The nights are warm for the time of year, with lows in the 60s. Confidence: Medium-High

Friday is the last of this week’s summery days, with partly sunny skies and highs well into the 80s. A shower or thunderstorm is possible late as a cold front approaches. It’s partly cloudy at night, with lows in the 60s. Confidence: Medium

Some lingering clouds are possible early Saturday, along with a slight chance of a shower. Then high pressure builds in from the north, bringing clearing skies and cooler weather. Highs are likely near 70. We probably stay dry Sunday, though clouds could increase late ahead of the next storm system. Highs are probably again near 70. Confidence: Low-Medium

DC weather history for September 28

Unseasonable chill in 1984 brought the lowest September high on record, while in 2004 the remnants of Hurricane Jeanne delivered record rainfall and widespread flooding.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: So glad to say goodbye to the rain. Highs near 70 are an improvement, with maybe some sun late. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
